source.authors: Emily L. Mensch, Amila A. Dissanayake, Muraleedharan G. Nair, C. Michael Wagner
source.title: The effect of putrescine on space use and activity in sea lamprey (Petromyzon marinus)

value: putrescine drew a significantly higher avoidance response than the solvent in the individual two-choice assay (Dunn's test p = 0.04) and did not differ from either alarm cue treatment (full-body p = 0.99, skin p = 0.99)
units: categorical (Dunn's test on proportion of time on the stimulus side)
method: individual two-choice arena (1.22 m x 1.22 m test area within a 1.22 x 2.44 m HDPE arena), odour pumped at 20 mL per min into one side with a target dilution of 2:1,000,000 odour to lake water; 22 min trials in darkness (5 min acclimation, 5 min pre-stimulus, 2 min pumping, 10 min stimulus observation); preference = time on stimulus side divided by total time after first encounter with the stimulus, 50 per cent neutral; putrescine stock 0.08 mg (0.04 per cent of one skin extract) in 10 mL ethanol brought to 1 L with 50:50 DI water:ethanol; concentration reaching the arena after dilution not printed; composition of the solvent control not explicitly described in Methods; Kruskal-Wallis across the five treatments
conditions: wild-sourced: migratory sub-adult males trapped by U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service in the Cheboygan and Ocqueoc Rivers (Lake Huron tributaries, Michigan) or the St. Mary's River, held at Hammond Bay Biological Station in 1385 L tanks on flowing Lake Huron water; Experiment 1 June 2020; n per treatment: solvent 18, full-body alarm cue 13, skin alarm cue 19, putrescine 10, petromyzonacil 19; same-section results: odour effect on preference Kruskal-Wallis chi2(4) = 17.78, p = 0.001; petromyzonacil not different from solvent (Dunn p = 0.74); activity: odour effect ANOVA F4,74 = 4.493, p < 0.01, both alarm cues raised activity versus solvent, putrescine did not (Tukey p = 0.98); Experiment 2 (group raceway, 10 fish per trial, June to July 2021, putrescine 10^-4 M, n = 10; putrescine plus petromyzonacil n = 10; 10^-1 M putrescine n = 5; solvent n = 10; crude skin alarm cue n = 15; full-body alarm cue n = 10): Kruskal-Wallis chi2(5) = 39.59, p < 0.001, both alarm cues lowered time on the stimulus side, and putrescine treatments failed to exhibit avoidance responses (all three p = 0.99 versus solvent); the abstract concludes there is limited evidence that putrescine acts as a robust repellent
quote: Putrescine showed significantly higher avoidance response than the solvent (Dunn's test, p=0.04; Fig. 2), and was not significantly different than either alarm cue treatment (Dunn's test, full-body p=0.99 and skin p=0.99; Fig. 2).
note: Classification: behavioural_response, side choice in a two-choice arena to a single compound against a solvent, with the alarm cues as comparators; the Experiment 2 group assay gave no avoidance of putrescine, so the single-species result is mixed across assays and the value is limited to Experiment 1. source.authors: Luisa Amo, Isabel López-Rull, Iluminada Pagán, Constantino Macías García
source.title: Evidence that the house finch (Carpodacus mexicanus) uses scent to avoid omnivore mammals

value: most birds avoided the chamber containing opossum scent (8/10) but not the chamber containing a novel scent (3/10)
units: count of birds avoiding the scented chamber (first choice)
method: olfactometer with a central box and two choice chambers; each bird received the two scented airflows for 5 min, then the doors opened and the first chamber entered was recorded; one chamber held a water-soiled odourless control paper, the other either common opossum urine on absorbent paper (from four trapped opossums, two chicken-fed and two fish-fed) or a commercial cologne as novel scent; urine dose or volume not printed; scented papers frozen at -20 C and used under 2 h; stimulus side balanced across trials, treatments randomly assigned to birds; each bird tested once per experiment
conditions: wild-sourced: 35 adults (28 males, 7 females) captured in San Luis Potosi, Mexico, in February 2009, acclimatised about 2 months, tested in April 2009, released in May under SEMARNAT permits; Experiment 1 used 20 birds (13 males, 7 females), 10 trials per treatment (opossum scent n = 10, novel scent n = 10); the cut parenthesis in the quote is the treatment test (Z = -2.13, p = 0.03); same-section results: Experiment 2 with 20 males found similar numbers choosing the fish-fed (9/20) and the chicken-fed (11/20) opossum scent (Z = -0.45, p = 0.66), so predator diet did not matter; five males were used in both experiments; the Discussion reports birds chose the cologne side in 7 of 10 trials, a preference rather than avoidance
where: Results, Detection of chemical cues of a nest predator (Experiment 1, Figure 2)
quote: The scent of the experimental chamber determined whether birds avoid it or not [...], as most birds avoided the experimental chamber, when it contained opossum scent (8/10), but not when it contained a novel scent (3/10).
note: Classification: behavioural_response, first-chamber choice against an odourless control with a novel-scent comparator; no other modality tested in the olfactometer (dim light, silent room). Predator is a mammalian omnivore (common opossum), the urine was taken from wild-trapped opossums.
